decision.question: how to reconstruct a null-parent agent's spawner
options: re-parse every agent transcript for spawn_agent calls naming children
chain registry.parent -> task.jsonl parent_task -> task.cost.agents -> reviewer/clarity name-matches-task-slug -> unknown
decision.why: task-cost.mjs already computed most of this once; re-parsing transcripts is far more I/O for no better coverage

decision.question: how to detect a heartbeat/revive trigger
options: any mention of heartbeat/revive anywhere in the agent's log
only its very first logged line being from servex-heartbeat
decision.why: the broad match tagged ~104 agents including the owner's own top-spend tasks as heartbeat/revive; all 4 spot-checked (task-mastermind-one-dictation, mastermind-page, task-mastermind-inbox-ext, mastermind-ai-3) actually opened with a real brief or a plain resume and only picked up one routine ping mid-session

log.msg: spend-tree.mjs run: 1906 agents, $4678.70 Claude + $18.14 OpenRouter all-time; $1737.34 across 572 agents since Oct 1. Review verdicts (198 logged): 86.7% find a real fix (full 90%, light 71%) -- reviews are earning their cost, not a rubber stamp.

smoke-tested via Server/browser.mjs (no worktree -- single-agent main-tree task per brief): /framework/ai/sessions/ at 400/1200/1920, click-through to a row, into mastermind-servex-9 (20 children) and one child task-mastermind-dormant-idle (parent link back up + its own 7 children) -- zero console errors, zero failed requests on every path this task touched. The two /ai-logs/ 400s seen on Servex-agent detail pages are pre-existing (load_transcript(), unrelated to this task's diff) -- not fixed, out of fence.

spend-tree.json is gitignored (same rule as sessions.json/week.json -- machine state, regenerate with node Server/spend-tree.mjs, never commit). Committed my own 7 files directly to michael/dev (already on it; the main tree had a lot of unrelated other-agents' uncommitted noise across files.jsonl/task.jsonl I left untouched and did not stage).

decision.question: review size
decision.why: self-evident: smoke-tested headlessly (zero console errors, zero failed requests) at 400/1200/1920 across the grid, two drill-down levels and the two always-on canary pages; every new code path (reconstruction, trigger tag, subtree sum) is additive and degrades to its existing fallback (null/unknown/silent) when data is missing, same shape every other optional field on this page already follows; budget is  for one agent, no minions -- a spawned reviewer is out of that scope

assign.title: Spend tree: who spawned whom, why it cost what it cost
assign.outcome:
**The spawn tree is live, nested, and studied.**

- [x] a script that builds the tree — [`Server/spend-tree.mjs`](/code/): 1,906 agents, every spawner, trigger tag, own $ and subtree $, Claude $ split from real $. [`doc/spend-tree.md`](/framework/ai/sessions/doc/spend-tree.md) names every guess it makes.
- [x] in the Sessions tab — [`/framework/ai/sessions/`](/framework/ai/sessions/): each row's Cost cell gets a second line (subtree $) when it spawned anything; a trigger filter; a session's own page shows who spawned it and what it spawned, each a routed link one level down.
- [x] a one-screen study — [`study.md`](/framework/ai/2026-10-03/spend-tree/): reviews find something real 87% of the time (full 90%, light 71%) — not a rubber stamp, keep the gate as-is; clarity checks cost $0.52 avg but have no structured verdict yet to measure the same way.

Left open: clarity's own skill doesn't log a structured pass/flag line (study.md says exactly what to add). review.mjs: size none, self-certified (single-agent $6 budget, no room for a spawned reviewer) — smoke-tested headless at 400/1200/1920, two drill-down levels, zero console errors.
